You are working in the git repo /workspace (a nand2tetris "Elements of Computing Systems" project skeleton).

ABSOLUTE RULES:
- You may ONLY create/modify files under /workspace/agent_tests/. NEVER touch anything under /workspace/projects/ or /workspace/requirements/ (read-only reference).
- Do NOT run git commit / git add. Do not modify git state.
- Python 3 only, standard library only (no pip installs, no pytest dependency - plain scripts with a main()).
- An HDL simulator ALREADY EXISTS and works: /workspace/agent_tests/hdl/simulator.py (class Simulator: set_pin/get_pin/eval_all/tick/tock/get_internal/set_internal/find_chip) and /workspace/agent_tests/hdl/builtins.py (built-in chip set). READ BOTH FIRST and reuse them; fix bugs in them only if you find real defects (report any fix).
- Test scripts (.tst) and expected outputs (.cmp) live next to the chips under /workspace/projects/01..05. The .cmp files use CRLF line endings in some cases - normalize by stripping trailing \r and trailing whitespace-insensitive compare is NOT allowed except for line-ending normalization.


Official nand2tetris .tst semantics you must implement faithfully:
- Comments: // to end of line, and /* ... */ blocks.
- A script is a sequence of commands separated by ',' and terminated by ';' (a ';' ends a "simulation step"; several steps may share a line).
- Commands: load <file>.hdl | output-file <f> | compare-to <f> | output-list <spec>... | set <pin|internal> <value> | eval | output | tick | tock | ticktock | repeat <n> { ... } | repeat { ... } (unbounded -> cap it) | while <lhs> <op> <rhs> { ... } | echo "..." | clear-echo | breakpoint ... | <ChipName> load <file> (e.g. "ROM32K load Add.hack").
- 'set' targets: a chip pin (in, load, address, instruction, reset, ...) OR internal state of a built-in part: RAM16K[0], ARegister[0], DRegister[], PC[], RAM[3] etc. Name in brackets = index into that built-in's state (empty brackets = index 0). Use Simulator.set_internal/get_internal.
- Value literals: plain signed decimal (-1, 12345), %B0011.. (binary), %X2000 (hex), %D-5 (decimal). Values are stored as unsigned bit patterns of the pin width (two's complement for negatives).
- output-list spec: name%Fa.b.c  where F in {B,D,X,S}; a = left pad spaces, b = field width, c = right pad spaces.
  * Column text = a spaces + formatted(b) + c spaces, columns separated by '|', line starts and ends with '|'.
  * D = decimal, right-aligned in b, interpreted SIGNED using the pin's bit width (e.g. 16-bit 0xFFFF -> -1).
  * B = binary, exactly b bits, least-significant b bits of the value, no padding spaces inside.
  * X = hex, exactly ceil(b) hex digits right-aligned zero-padded (verify against any %X usage in the repo; if unused, best effort).
  * S = string, LEFT-aligned in b (used for 'time').
  * The header line (written once, before any output line) contains each pin's display name CENTERED in width (a+b+c) with the extra space biased to the RIGHT (left pad = floor((width-len)/2)), truncated to the first 'width' chars if too long. Verify against real headers, e.g. projects/05/CPU.cmp header "|time| inM  |  instruction   |reset| outM  |writeM |addre| pc  |DRegiste|" from output-list "time%S0.4.0 inM%D0.6.0 instruction%B0.16.0 reset%B2.1.2 outM%D1.6.0 writeM%B3.1.3 addressM%D0.5.0 pc%D0.5.0 DRegister[]%D1.6.1".
- The special output column 'time': starts at 0. After 'tick' it renders "<n>+"; after 'tock' it renders "<n+1>" and n increments. Before any tick it renders "<n>". Confirmed by projects/03/a/Bit.cmp ("| 0+   |", "| 1    |", "| 1+   |", "| 2    |") and projects/05/ComputerAdd.cmp (first output before any tick is "| 0    |").
- Comparison to .cmp: line by line; the character '*' in the .cmp file is a WILDCARD matching any single character (projects/05/CPU.cmp uses "*******" for unchecked outM). Report the first mismatching line with both texts and the line number.


TASK: Build the HDL test-script runner.

Deliverables:
1. /workspace/agent_tests/hdl/tst.py - the .tst interpreter/runner library (parse + execute + format + compare), built on hdl/simulator.py.
2. /workspace/agent_tests/run_hdl_tests.py - CLI: `python3 agent_tests/run_hdl_tests.py <paths...>` where each path is a .tst file or a directory (recurse for *.tst). Prints one line per test: "PASS <path>" or "FAIL <path>: <reason / first diff>", then a summary "N passed, M failed". Exit code 1 if any failed. Support --timeout per test and skip/report chips whose HDL is still a "// TODO: implement" stub as "SKIP (stub)".
   IMPORTANT: write the generated output to the .out path named by the script but INSIDE a temp/scratch dir (e.g. /workspace/agent_tests/.out/<name>.out) so nothing under projects/ is ever written. projects/ must stay clean - verify with `git status --short projects` at the end (must be unchanged except pre-existing modifications to projects/01/*.hdl).
3. Extras needed for real scripts:
   - "while <lhs> <op> <rhs> { ... }" with ops <>, =, <, >, <=, >= comparing an output pin or internal value against a literal. projects/05/Memory.tst waits on the keyboard: `while out <> 75 { tick, tock, }`. Since there is no interactive user, implement this: when a while loop's condition can never change by ticking (i.e. it did not change after a few iterations) and the loaded chip contains a built-in 'Keyboard' instance, set that Keyboard's value to the literal from the condition (simulating the user pressing the key) and continue. Cap iterations (e.g. 200000) and fail loudly with a clear message rather than hanging.
   - "repeat { ... }" with no count: cap at a configurable number of iterations.
   - "<Chip> load <file>": load a .hack program into the named built-in instance (ROM32K.load_program already exists in builtins.py).
4. Self-verification you MUST run and report:
   a. /workspace/demo/Xor.tst against /workspace/demo/Xor.cmp -> must PASS (ground truth for formatting; note demo/Xor.hdl exists there).
   b. All of /workspace/projects/01/*.tst -> those chips are already implemented; they must all PASS. If any fails, first suspect YOUR runner, then report (do NOT edit the .hdl files - you are forbidden to).
   c. A synthetic negative test: prove the runner actually detects a wrong value (e.g. copy a chip into a scratch dir, break it, confirm FAIL). Keep it as agent_tests/test_runner_selfcheck.py.
Return: a concise report of what you built, the exact commands to run it, self-verification results (pass/fail counts), and any bug you fixed in simulator.py/builtins.py.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	"""A small HDL parser and event-driven simulator for the nand2tetris HDL.
2	
3	Chip resolution mirrors the official Hardware Simulator: a part name is looked
4	up as ``<Name>.hdl`` in the directory of the chip being loaded and, failing
5	that, resolves to the built-in implementation from ``builtins.py``.
6	
7	Buses are flattened to single-bit nodes.  Every leaf instance is a built-in;
8	user-defined chips are expanded in place with their pins aliased onto the
9	enclosing chip's nodes.  When one output pin feeds several wires
10	(``ALU(out=outM, out=aluOut)``) the wires are merged with a union-find pass
11	after expansion.
12	"""
13	
14	import os
15	import re
16	from collections import deque
17	
18	from . import builtins as bi
19	
20	CONST0 = 0
21	CONST1 = 1
22	
23	
24	class HDLError(Exception):
25	    pass
26	
27	
28	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
29	# parsing
30	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
31	
32	_COMMENT_RE = re.compile(r'//[^\n]*|/\*.*?\*/', re.S)
33	
34	
35	class PinDecl:
36	    __slots__ = ('name', 'width')
37	
38	    def __init__(self, name, width):
39	        self.name = name
40	        self.width = width
41	
42	
43	class Part:
44	    __slots__ = ('chip', 'conns')
45	
46	    def __init__(self, chip, conns):
47	        self.chip = chip
48	        self.conns = conns  # list of (pin, pin_slice, wire, wire_slice)
49	
50	
51	class ChipDef:
52	    def __init__(self, name, ins, outs, parts, path):
53	        self.name = name
54	        self.ins = ins
55	        self.outs = outs
56	        self.parts = parts
57	        self.path = path
58	        self.in_width = {p.name: p.width for p in ins}
59	        self.out_width = {p.name: p.width for p in outs}
60	
61	
62	def _strip_comments(text):
63	    return _COMMENT_RE.sub(' ', text)
64	
65	
66	def _parse_pin_list(text):
67	    pins = []
68	    for item in text.split(','):
69	        item = item.strip()
70	        if not item:
71	            continue
72	        m = re.fullmatch(r'([A-Za-z_][\w.]*)\s*(?:\[\s*(\d+)\s*\])?', item)
73	        if not m:
74	            raise HDLError('bad pin declaration: %r' % item)
75	        pins.append(PinDecl(m.group(1), int(m.group(2) or 1)))
76	    return pins
77	
78	
79	def _parse_ref(text):
80	    """Parse ``name``/``name[i]``/``name[i..j]`` into ``(name, slice_or_None)``."""
81	    text = text.strip()
82	    m = re.fullmatch(
83	        r'([A-Za-z_][\w.]*)\s*(?:\[\s*(\d+)\s*(?:\.\.\s*(\d+)\s*)?\])?', text)
84	    if not m:
85	        raise HDLError('bad pin reference: %r' % text)
86	    name = m.group(1)
87	    if m.group(2) is None:
88	        return name, None
89	    lo = int(m.group(2))
90	    hi = int(m.group(3)) if m.group(3) is not None else lo
91	    if hi < lo:
92	        raise HDLError('inverted bus range: %r' % text)
93	    return name, (lo, hi)
94	
95	
96	def parse_hdl(path):
97	    with open(path) as fh:
98	        text = _strip_comments(fh.read())
99	
100	    m = re.search(r'CHIP\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\{(.*)\}', text, re.S)
101	    if not m:
102	        raise HDLError('%s: no CHIP definition found' % path)
103	    name, body = m.group(1), m.group(2)
104	
105	    ins, outs = [], []
106	    m_in = re.search(r'\bIN\b(.*?);', body, re.S)
107	    if m_in:
108	        ins = _parse_pin_list(m_in.group(1))
109	    m_out = re.search(r'\bOUT\b(.*?);', body, re.S)
110	    if m_out:
111	        outs = _parse_pin_list(m_out.group(1))
112	
113	    m_parts = re.search(r'\bPARTS:\s*(.*)$', body, re.S)
114	    parts_text = m_parts.group(1) if m_parts else ''
115	    if 'TODO' in parts_text:
116	        raise HDLError('%s: chip body is still a stub' % path)
117	    parts = []
118	    for stmt in parts_text.split(';'):
119	        stmt = stmt.strip()
120	        if not stmt:
121	            continue
122	        pm = re.fullmatch(r'([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\((.*)\)', stmt, re.S)
123	        if not pm:
124	            raise HDLError('%s: cannot parse part %r' % (path, stmt))
125	        chip = pm.group(1)
126	        conns = []
127	        for conn in pm.group(2).split(','):
128	            conn = conn.strip()
129	            if not conn:
130	                continue
131	            if '=' not in conn:
132	                raise HDLError('%s: bad connection %r' % (path, conn))
133	            left, right = conn.split('=', 1)
134	            pin, pin_sl = _parse_ref(left)
135	            wire, wire_sl = _parse_ref(right)
136	            conns.append((pin, pin_sl, wire, wire_sl))
137	        parts.append(Part(chip, conns))
138	    return ChipDef(name, ins, outs, parts, path)
139	
140	
141	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
142	# netlist
143	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
144	
145	class Instance:
146	    __slots__ = ('chip', 'kind', 'fn', 'obj', 'ins', 'outs', 'index')
147	
148	    def __init__(self, chip, kind, fn, obj, ins, outs, index):
149	        self.chip = chip
150	        self.kind = kind          # 'comb' or 'seq'
151	        self.fn = fn
152	        self.obj = obj
153	        self.ins = ins            # {pin: [node, ...]} LSB first
154	        self.outs = outs
155	        self.index = index
156	
157	
158	class Simulator:
159	    """Loads a chip from an .hdl file and simulates it."""
160	
161	    MAX_STEPS = 5000000
162	
163	    def __init__(self, hdl_path, search_dirs=None):
164	        self.hdl_path = os.path.abspath(hdl_path)
165	        self.dir = os.path.dirname(self.hdl_path)
166	        self.search_dirs = [self.dir] + [os.path.abspath(d)
167	                                         for d in (search_dirs or [])]
168	        self._chip_cache = {}
169	        self.values = [0, 1]
170	        self._parent = [0, 1]
171	        self.instances = []
172	        self.by_chip = {}
173	        self.readers = {}
174	
175	        self.chip = self._load_chip_file(self.hdl_path)
176	        self.pin_nodes = {}
177	        for p in self.chip.ins:
178	            self.pin_nodes[p.name] = self._new_nodes(p.width)
179	        for p in self.chip.outs:
180	            self.pin_nodes[p.name] = self._new_nodes(p.width)
181	        self.pin_width = dict(self.chip.in_width)
182	        self.pin_width.update(self.chip.out_width)
183	        self.input_pins = {p.name for p in self.chip.ins}
184	        self._expand(self.chip, self.pin_nodes)
185	        self._finalize()
186	        self.seq_indices = [i for i, inst in enumerate(self.instances)
187	                            if inst.kind == 'seq']
188	        self.eval_all()
189	
190	    # -- nodes ------------------------------------------------------------
191	    def _new_node(self):
192	        self.values.append(0)
193	        self._parent.append(len(self.values) - 1)
194	        return len(self.values) - 1
195	
196	    def _new_nodes(self, n):
197	        return [self._new_node() for _ in range(n)]
198	
199	    def _find(self, n):
200	        p = self._parent
201	        root = n
202	        while p[root] != root:
203	            root = p[root]
204	        while p[n] != root:
205	            p[n], n = root, p[n]
206	        return root
207	
208	    def _union(self, a, b):
209	        ra, rb = self._find(a), self._find(b)
210	        if ra == rb:
211	            return
212	        # keep the lower id (so constants 0/1 always win) as representative
213	        if rb < ra:
214	            ra, rb = rb, ra
215	        self._parent[rb] = ra
216	
217	    # -- chip resolution --------------------------------------------------
218	    def _load_chip_file(self, path):
219	        if path not in self._chip_cache:
220	            self._chip_cache[path] = parse_hdl(path)
221	        return self._chip_cache[path]
222	
223	    def _resolve(self, name):
224	        """Return a ChipDef for a user chip, or None when it is built-in."""
225	        for d in self.search_dirs:
226	            cand = os.path.join(d, name + '.hdl')
227	            if os.path.exists(cand):
228	                return self._load_chip_file(cand)
229	        if bi.is_builtin(name):
230	            return None
231	        raise HDLError('unknown chip: %s' % name)
232	
233	    def _interface(self, name):
234	        chip = self._resolve(name)
235	        if chip is None:
236	            ins, outs = bi.builtin_interface(name)
237	            return ({n: w for n, w in ins}, {n: w for n, w in outs}, None)
238	        return (dict(chip.in_width), dict(chip.out_width), chip)
239	
240	    # -- expansion --------------------------------------------------------
241	    def _add_instance(self, chip, ins, outs):
242	        idx = len(self.instances)
243	        if chip in bi.COMBINATIONAL:
244	            _, _, fn = bi.COMBINATIONAL[chip]
245	            inst = Instance(chip, 'comb', fn, None, ins, outs, idx)
246	        else:
247	            inst = Instance(chip, 'seq', None, bi.SEQUENTIAL[chip](),
248	                            ins, outs, idx)
249	        self.instances.append(inst)
250	        self.by_chip.setdefault(chip, []).append(inst)
251	        return inst
252	
253	    def _expand(self, chip, pin_nodes):
254	        wires = dict(pin_nodes)
255	        widths = {}
256	        for p in chip.ins:
257	            widths[p.name] = p.width
258	        for p in chip.outs:
259	            widths[p.name] = p.width
260	
261	        parts_meta = []
262	        for part in chip.parts:
263	            in_w, out_w, sub = self._interface(part.chip)
264	            parts_meta.append((part, in_w, out_w, sub))
265	            for pin, pin_sl, wire, wire_sl in part.conns:
266	                if wire in ('true', 'false'):
267	                    continue
268	                if pin in in_w:
269	                    pw = in_w[pin]
270	                elif pin in out_w:
271	                    pw = out_w[pin]

279	        for name, w in sorted(widths.items()):
280	            if name not in wires:
281	                wires[name] = self._new_nodes(w)

283	        def wire_nodes(wire, wire_sl, span):
284	            if wire == 'true':
285	                return [CONST1] * span
286	            if wire == 'false':
287	                return [CONST0] * span
288	            nodes = wires[wire]
289	            if wire_sl is None:
290	                sel = nodes[:span]
291	            else:
292	                sel = nodes[wire_sl[0]:wire_sl[1] + 1]
293	            if len(sel) != span:
294	                raise HDLError('%s: width mismatch on wire %s (%d vs %d)'
295	                               % (chip.name, wire, len(sel), span))
296	            return sel

298	        for part, in_w, out_w, sub in parts_meta:
299	            sub_in = {p: [CONST0] * w for p, w in in_w.items()}
300	            out_conns = {}
301	            for pin, pin_sl, wire, wire_sl in part.conns:
302	                if pin in in_w:
303	                    pw = in_w[pin]
304	                    lo, hi = (pin_sl if pin_sl else (0, pw - 1))
305	                    src = wire_nodes(wire, wire_sl, hi - lo + 1)
306	                    cur = sub_in[pin]
307	                    sub_in[pin] = cur[:lo] + src + cur[hi + 1:]
308	                else:
309	                    pw = out_w[pin]
310	                    lo, hi = (pin_sl if pin_sl else (0, pw - 1))
311	                    dst = wire_nodes(wire, wire_sl, hi - lo + 1)
312	                    out_conns.setdefault(pin, []).append((lo, dst))
313	
314	            sub_out = {}
315	            for pin, w in out_w.items():
316	                nodes = [None] * w
317	                for lo, dst in out_conns.get(pin, []):
318	                    for i, n in enumerate(dst):
319	                        if nodes[lo + i] is None:
320	                            nodes[lo + i] = n
321	                        else:
322	                            self._union(nodes[lo + i], n)

328	            if sub is None:

330	            else:

332	                child_pins.update(sub_out)

335	    def _finalize(self):
336	        f = self._find
337	        for inst in self.instances:
338	            inst.ins = {p: [f(n) for n in nodes]
339	                        for p, nodes in inst.ins.items()}
340	            inst.outs = {p: [f(n) for n in nodes]
341	                         for p, nodes in inst.outs.items()}
342	        self.pin_nodes = {p: [f(n) for n in nodes]
343	                          for p, nodes in self.pin_nodes.items()}
344	        readers = {}
345	        for inst in self.instances:
346	            seen = set()
347	            for nodes in inst.ins.values():
348	                for n in nodes:
349	                    if n not in seen:
350	                        seen.add(n)
351	                        readers.setdefault(n, []).append(inst.index)
352	        self.readers = readers
353	
354	    # -- evaluation -------------------------------------------------------
355	    def _read(self, nodes):
356	        v = 0
357	        values = self.values
358	        for i, n in enumerate(nodes):
359	            if values[n]:
360	                v |= 1 << i
361	        return v
362	
363	    def _propagate(self, seeds):
364	        values = self.values
365	        instances = self.instances
366	        readers = self.readers
367	        queued = bytearray(len(instances))
368	        dq = deque()
369	        for i in seeds:
370	            if not queued[i]:
371	                queued[i] = 1
372	                dq.append(i)
373	        steps = 0
374	        while dq:
375	            steps += 1
376	            if steps > self.MAX_STEPS:
377	                raise HDLError('combinational loop detected in %s'
378	                               % self.chip.name)
379	            idx = dq.popleft()
380	            queued[idx] = 0
381	            inst = instances[idx]
382	            vals = {}
383	            for pin, nodes in inst.ins.items():
384	                v = 0
385	                for i, n in enumerate(nodes):
386	                    if values[n]:
387	                        v |= 1 << i
388	                vals[pin] = v
389	            outs = (inst.fn(vals) if inst.kind == 'comb'
390	                    else inst.obj.combinational(vals))
391	            for pin, value in outs.items():
392	                for i, n in enumerate(inst.outs[pin]):
393	                    b = (value >> i) & 1
394	                    if values[n] != b:
395	                        values[n] = b
396	                        for r in readers.get(n, ()):
397	                            if not queued[r]:
398	                                queued[r] = 1
399	                                dq.append(r)
400	        return steps
401	
402	    def eval_all(self):
403	        self._propagate(range(len(self.instances)))
404	
405	    eval = eval_all

407	    def set_pin(self, name, value):
408	        if name not in self.pin_nodes:
409	            raise HDLError('%s: no such pin: %s' % (self.chip.name, name))
410	        nodes = self.pin_nodes[name]
411	        seeds = []
412	        for i, n in enumerate(nodes):
413	            b = (value >> i) & 1
414	            if self.values[n] != b:
415	                self.values[n] = b
416	                seeds.extend(self.readers.get(n, ()))
417	        self._propagate(seeds)
418	
419	    def get_pin(self, name):
420	        return self._read(self.pin_nodes[name])
421	
422	    def tick(self):
423	        for i in self.seq_indices:
424	            inst = self.instances[i]
425	            vals = {pin: self._read(nodes) for pin, nodes in inst.ins.items()}
426	            inst.obj.clock_up(vals)
427	
428	    def tock(self):
429	        for i in self.seq_indices:
430	            self.instances[i].obj.clock_down()
431	        self._propagate(self.seq_indices)
432	
433	    # -- internal state access -------------------------------------------
434	    def find_chip(self, name):
435	        insts = self.by_chip.get(name)
436	        if not insts:
437	            raise HDLError('no built-in %s instance inside %s'
438	                           % (name, self.chip.name))
439	        return insts[0].obj
440	
441	    def get_internal(self, name, index):
442	        return self.find_chip(name).get_value(index)
443	
444	    def set_internal(self, name, index, value):
445	        self.find_chip(name).set_value(value, index)
446	        self.eval_all()

1	"""Native ("built-in") implementations of the standard nand2tetris chip set.
2	
3	The official Hardware Simulator resolves a chip-part name by looking for
4	`<Name>.hdl` in the directory of the chip being loaded; when that file does
5	not exist it falls back to the built-in implementation.  This module supplies
6	those built-in implementations so the same resolution rule can be used here.
7	
8	Conventions
9	-----------
10	* Pin values are plain Python ints holding an unsigned bit pattern.
11	* Combinational chips are described by ``COMBINATIONAL[name] = (ins, outs, fn)``
12	  where ``ins``/``outs`` are ``[(pin, width), ...]`` and ``fn`` maps a dict of
13	  input values to a dict of output values.
14	* Clocked chips are classes exposing ``combinational``, ``clock_up`` and
15	  ``clock_down`` (see ``SequentialChip``).
16	"""
17	
18	W16 = 0xFFFF
19	
20	
21	def _mask(v, width):
22	    return v & ((1 << width) - 1)
23	
24	
25	def _bits16(v):
26	    return [(v >> i) & 1 for i in range(16)]
27	
28	
29	def _from_bits(bits):
30	    v = 0
31	    for i, b in enumerate(bits):
32	        if b:
33	            v |= 1 << i
34	    return v
35	
36	
37	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
38	# combinational built-ins
39	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
40	
41	COMBINATIONAL = {}
42	
43	
44	def _comb(name, ins, outs):
45	    def deco(fn):
46	        COMBINATIONAL[name] = (ins, outs, fn)
47	        return fn
48	    return deco
49	
50	
51	@_comb('Nand', [('a', 1), ('b', 1)], [('out', 1)])
52	def _nand(v):
53	    return {'out': 1 - (v['a'] & v['b'])}
54	
55	
56	@_comb('Not', [('in', 1)], [('out', 1)])
57	def _not(v):
58	    return {'out': 1 - v['in']}
59	
60	
61	@_comb('And', [('a', 1), ('b', 1)], [('out', 1)])
62	def _and(v):
63	    return {'out': v['a'] & v['b']}
64	
65	
66	@_comb('Or', [('a', 1), ('b', 1)], [('out', 1)])
67	def _or(v):
68	    return {'out': v['a'] | v['b']}
69

166	@_comb('ALU',
167	       [('x', 16), ('y', 16), ('zx', 1), ('nx', 1),
168	        ('zy', 1), ('ny', 1), ('f', 1), ('no', 1)],
169	       [('out', 16), ('zr', 1), ('ng', 1)])
170	def _alu(v):
171	    x, y = v['x'], v['y']
172	    if v['zx']:
173	        x = 0
174	    if v['nx']:
175	        x = (~x) & W16
176	    if v['zy']:
177	        y = 0
178	    if v['ny']:
179	        y = (~y) & W16
180	    out = (x + y) & W16 if v['f'] else (x & y)
181	    if v['no']:
182	        out = (~out) & W16
183	    return {'out': out,
184	            'zr': 1 if out == 0 else 0,

192	class SequentialChip:
193	    """Base class for clocked built-in chips.
194	
195	    Timing follows the official simulator: ``clock_up`` (tick) latches the
196	    inputs without changing any output, ``clock_down`` (tock) commits the
197	    latched value so that it becomes visible on the outputs.

200	    INS = []

203	    def combinational(self, v):

// This file is part of www.nand2tetris.org
// and the book "The Elements of Computing Systems"
// by Nisan and Schocken, MIT Press.
// File name: projects/demo/Xor.hdl

/**
 *  Exclusive-or gate: true if either a is true and b is false, or
 *  a is false and b is true; false otherwise.
 *  QUESTION: how can the simulator execute this program properly without
 *  HDL implementations of the underlying Not, And, and Or chip-parts?
 *  Answer: since the demo folder contains no Not.hdl, And.hdl and Or.hdl
 *  files, the simulator reverts to using their built-in implementations.
 */

CHIP Xor {
    IN a, b;
    OUT out;

    PARTS:
    Not (in=a, out=nota);
    Not (in=b, out=notb);
    And (a=a, b=notb, out=x);
    And (a=nota, b=b, out=y);
    Or (a=x, b=y, out=out);
}
